study.question: Does own-event allocation of inverse-norm product gradients help validation ranking beyond their within-history average or scale distribution? Observed limitation: fixed tangent AUC .6149888455418249 is only .000007154362010153292 above full .6149816911798147 and has .00001284768903553335 worse Logloss. First-512 fixed-tangent diagnostics show scale mean .1878697276/std .0605802052 and category-match versus no-match means .1432671845/.1914683729, but these are checkpoint-specific descriptive aggregates, not measured within-history variation or training-gradient evidence. The existing constant replacement changes both scale allocation and heterogeneity. This phase cannot select new seeds; the proposed source-audited replacement controls resolve an attribution gap without silently changing the frozen protocol.
study.hypothesis: Provisional optimization hypothesis: event-specific inverse-norm allocation is unnecessary or mildly adverse under the current Adam recipe, while a detached within-history mean can preserve useful impression-level scale variation and remove unnecessary event-level heterogeneity. Expect history_mean to exceed full and fixed in AUC and reassignment not to be consistently worse than full; either prediction can fail. The latter contrasts are conditional at seed 42, not repeated support, semantic causality or a novelty claim.

nearest_work.difference: Current candidate.py exactly matches the registered fixed-tangent source SHA256, and full/constant ancestor constructor, encoding, weights, logits and scoring ASTs match. Earlier trials already isolate scaling/projection at seed 42. Proposed difference is within-impression averaging and multiset-preserving reassignment of inverse scales. Historical full memory was resolved in full and reviewed by selected fields, including all seven trajectory branches, alternatives and limitations; hashes alone do not verify execution.

study.proposed_difference: Four standalone modules with identical executable AST except the CONFIG normalization_gradient default: full_replay and constant_replay controls, history_mean candidate, and history_reassigned allocation control. Only the product-channel surrogate backward scale changes. Row means exclude padding and floored events; reassignment packs valid regular events in supplied order then rotates by floor(n/2). Empty/singleton donor sets remain unchanged. Both are parameter-free, deterministic, within-row only and have no scale derivatives, added data or calibration. This adds a mechanism contrast instead of asserting another tiny selected-score gain; broader literature novelty is unverified. The earlier replication-first plan is retained as a deferred priority: current host seed is fixed at 42 and this action specifically requires a candidate, so seeds 43/44 are only reserved future work, not smuggled through config.
predictions: At the same finite state all four products and logits agree exactly apart from ordinary floating-point tolerance; parameter/state-key layout and initialization draw order match the existing aligned models. Full and fixed controls should reproduce their historical validation scores at the frozen seed, conditional on host determinism.

CPU float64 product-channel VJP scaled errors should be <=1e-8 for every tested mode/probe, including zero/floor/boundary cases. Same-state product/logit errors and padding/empty-summary errors should be <=2e-6. Check diagnostic counts; synthetic boundary count must be positive.

On first-512 rows, mean replacement preserves the per-row sum of regular scales; reassignment preserves both the sum and squared sum within relative 1e-5. Report within-history standard deviation, reassignment magnitude/correlation, singleton/empty/floor counts rather than assuming a meaningful perturbation.

If the hypothesis is right, history_mean-minus-full and history_mean-minus-constant validation AUC will be positive. Reassignment should not show a clear own-event advantage for full in this seed; all deltas and loss/cost tradeoffs are reported, with no invented noninferiority margin.

Preexisting hour/history-length/action/frequency/category-match slices remain exploratory with sample and class counts; no new validation-chosen bins or positive-only subgroup reporting. First-512 diagnostics do not establish population field-semantic or missing/unseen-field performance.
falsifiers: A failed same-state forward, masking, scale preservation, boundary or VJP check invalidates implementation-based attribution regardless of AUC. Material replay drift requires an isolation audit; source hash matching alone is insufficient.

A nonpositive history_mean-minus-full AUC contradicts improvement by this averaging implementation at seed 42; a nonpositive history_mean-minus-fixed AUC contradicts the proposed extra benefit from retained impression-level variation in this run. Loss reversals refute uniform metric superiority.

A positive full-minus-reassigned AUC weakens the dispensability prediction; negligible reassignment magnitude or strongly retained within-history correlation makes the control weak rather than a mechanism refutation.

Future paired reversals/nonpositive mean improvements at seeds 43/44 weaken repeatability. No statistical significance, equivalence, necessity, sufficiency or semantic mediation can be established from this round alone.
alternative_explanations: One fixed seed with adaptive validation reuse; no user-cluster intervals, independent repetitions or equivalence claim.
Scale targets evolve with learned embeddings, so per-step distribution matching at a fixed state does not match distributions between fitted checkpoints.

Only the product-channel backward route is changed; shared embeddings also receive gradients through unnormalized history, queries and static features. This does not identify semantic mediation or match Adam updates.

Training and validation aggregates cannot verify identical initialization, data order, optimizer state or checkpoint identities. Source/host diagnostics narrow this gap but do not independently audit execution.

A single moderate global step scale may suffice; neither event-specific nor within-history adaptivity need help. Existing fixed-identity proximity and projection-by-scale interaction support retaining this possibility.
Norm/direction correlations, Adam conditioning or shared embedding adaptation can explain differences without field-semantic relevance; matched forward scalars do not match optimizer updates.

A deterministic temporal rotation may preserve or introduce action/recency associations; it changes allocation without guaranteeing independent donors. Compare measured within-history correlation before interpreting nulls.
Total sampled scale variance can be entirely between histories; without actual within-history variation the new controls have no discriminating power.

Parameter equality does not imply equal compute: reductions/packing add work. Report actual wall/training seconds, throughput, latency and peak memory; no equal-compute or efficiency claim without measured controls.
